statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows moderate correlations (r≈0.3) between baseline HRV and stress-evoked physiological changes, translating to moderate effects on model uncertainty.
minimum_data_needed: N=120 participants aged 18-45
5-min seated baseline ECG/PPG to compute resting RMSSD
Standardized psychosocial stress task (TSST) with PPG recording
Model prediction entropy for each stress vs non-stress segment
Covariates: age, sex, VO2max, caffeine intake, medication status
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher resting RMSSD will be associated with higher model prediction entropy (positive association).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for age, sex, VO2max, caffeine, and medication, the regression coefficient for resting RMSSD is not significantly positive (p>0.05) or is negative.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects model: entropy ~ resting_RMSSD + age + sex + VO2max + caffeine + medication + (1|subject). Test significance of resting_RMSSD coefficient via Wald test.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Assumes stable baseline RMSSD across sessions; can be verified with intraclass correlation.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Skin impedance explains a notable portion of PPG SNR variance in pilot studies (R²≈0.25), suggesting a medium effect on downstream uncertainty.
minimum_data_needed: N=100 participants
Skin impedance measured at sensor site (kΩ) using device electrodes
PPG AC amplitude and SNR computed
Model prediction entropy
Control variables: skin hydration, ambient temperature, hair presence, lotion use, sweat rate
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher skin impedance will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After controlling for skin hydration, ambient temperature, hair, lotion, sweat, the impedance coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Multiple linear regression: entropy ~ skin_impedance + skin_hydration + ambient_temp + hair_removal + lotion_use + sweat_rate. Evaluate impedance coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Impedance can be measured concurrently with PPG; ensure stable temperature.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Circadian misalignment effects on physiological reactivity are often subtle (Cohen's d≈0.2), leading to a small effect on model uncertainty.
minimum_data_needed: N=80 participants with stable sleep-wake schedule ≥3 days
Circadian phase assessed via melatonin onset (DLMO) or core body temperature
Clock time of each measurement
Compute absolute phase difference (hours)
Model prediction entropy
Covariates: sleep duration, caffeine, chronotype, recent stressor, light exposure
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Larger absolute circadian phase difference will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for sleep deprivation, caffeine, chronotype, recent stress, and light, the phase difference coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects model: entropy ~ abs_phase_diff + sleep_hours + caffeine + chronotype + recent_stressor + lux + (1|subject). Test abs_phase_diff coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: If melatonin assay unavailable, use actigraphy-derived phase as proxy; note increased measurement error.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Label noise from self-report bias can substantially degrade classifier performance; prior EMA-physiology disagreement studies show moderate impact (AUC drop ~0.1).
minimum_data_needed: N=90 participants
EMA prompts 6x/day for 2 weeks
Physiological ground truth from validated stress inducer (e.g., cold pressor) to compute label noise per subject
Self-report bias score (e.g., ICC between EMA and physiology)
Model prediction entropy
Control variables: neuroticism, social desirability, momentary affect, working memory, language proficiency
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher self-report bias score will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After controlling for neuroticism, social desirability, momentary affect, working memory, language proficiency, the bias coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Multiple regression: entropy ~ bias_score + neuroticism + social_desirability + PANAS + WM + language_prof. Test bias_score coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Bias score can be derived from intraclass correlation coefficient; ensure EMA compliance >80%.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Strap tightness influences motion artifact but effect sizes are often modest due to algorithmic correction; pilot data show small correlations (r≈0.15).
minimum_data_needed: N=110 participants
Strap tightness measured via force sensor (N) during rest and 6‑min walk test
Motion artifact index (accelerometer variance)
PPG SNR
Model prediction entropy
Control variables: arm circumference, fat thickness, skin elasticity, movement variance, strap usage duration
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Lower strap tightness will be associated with higher model prediction entropy (inverse relationship).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for arm circumference, fat thickness, skin elasticity, movement variance, and strap usage, the tightness coefficient is not significantly negative (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects model: entropy ~ tightness + arm_circ + fat_thick + skin_elastic + movement_var + strap_days + (1|subject). Test tightness coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: If force sensor unavailable, use PPG amplitude variability as proxy; note reduced precision.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: COMT Val158Met explains a small fraction of variance in stress reactivity (η²≈0.02), leading to a small effect on wearable uncertainty.
minimum_data_needed: N=250 participants (to detect small genetic effect)
Genotyping for COMT Val158Met (0‑2 Val alleles)
Stress task (mental arithmetic or TSST) with ECG/PPG ≥256 Hz
Stress‑evoked HRV change (ΔRMSSD)
Model prediction entropy
Control variables: baseline dopamine, recent stress exposure, medication affecting catecholamines, MAOA genotype, ancestry PCs
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Each additional Val allele will be associated with higher model prediction entropy (positive dose‑response).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for baseline dopamine, recent stress, medication, MAOA, ancestry, the Val allele coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: entropy ~ Val_allele_count + baseline_dopamine + recent_stress + med_status + MAOA + PC1-PC5. Test Val_allele_count coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Large N required for adequate power; consider adding interaction with stress task intensity.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Longitudinal habituation/sensitization can produce moderate changes in stress response over weeks (Cohen's d≈0.4), translating to a medium effect on uncertainty.
minimum_data_needed: N=70 participants
Weekly lab sessions ≥8 weeks with standardized stressor
Wearable compliance >90%
Compute within‑subject stress‑response slope (ΔRMSSD per session) via mixed‑effects
Model prediction entropy per session
Control variables: life event checklist, medication changes, PSQI trend, ambient temperature, firmware version
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Greater absolute change in stress‑response slope across sessions will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for life events, medication changes, sleep quality, temperature, firmware, the slope‑change coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects model: entropy ~ abs_slope_change + life_event_score + med_change + PSQI_trend + avg_temp + firmware + (1|subject). Test abs_slope_change coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Slope change can be estimated as subject-specific random slope variance; alternative is to include session*subject interaction.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Activity context confounding has shown moderate impact on stress classification (AUC reduction ~0.08) in free‑living studies.
minimum_data_needed: N=100 participants
7‑day free‑living monitoring with accelerometer 30 Hz
Compute average daily activity intensity (MET‑hours) and proportion time in moderate‑vigorous activity
Model prediction entropy (context‑agnostic)
Control variables: VO2max, resting RMSSD, exercise‑induced ΔRMSSD, daily caffeine, proportion activity morning vs evening
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher average daily activity intensity will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for VO2max, resting RMSSD, exercise‑induced ΔRMSSD, caffeine, and time‑of‑day activity, the activity intensity coefficient is not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Multiple regression: entropy ~ avg_MET_hours + VO2max + resting_RMSSD + exercise_delta_RMSSD + daily_caffeine + prop_morning_activity. Test avg_MET_hours coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Including activity as covariate in model should reduce entropy if hypothesis holds; can test interaction.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Parameter uncertainty scales inversely with sample size; simulations show that halving labeled samples can double predictive variance, indicating a large effect.
minimum_data_needed: N=60 participants with varying numbers of labeled stress samples per subject (range 5‑50)
Same regularized logistic regression hyperparameters for all subjects
Labels from validated stress inductions
Compute posterior variance of classifier weights (or predictive variance) per subject
Model prediction uncertainty (predictive variance)
Control variables: label variance, label reliability (kappa), regularization lambda, class imbalance, mean stress intensity
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Fewer labeled samples per subject will be associated with higher model prediction uncertainty (inverse relationship).
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After controlling for label variance, label reliability, regularization strength, class imbalance, and stress intensity, the sample size coefficient is not significantly negative (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: uncertainty ~ n_i + label_variance + kappa + lambda + class_ratio + stress_intensity. Test n_i coefficient.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Can be confirmed by simulation: subsample labels and measure resulting uncertainty.

statistical_testability_builds.effect_size_rationale: Sampling jitter and sync offsets typically contribute minor noise relative to biological variability; pilot data show small effects on classification confidence (r≈0.1).
minimum_data_needed: N=80 participants
Device firmware logs timestamps with µs resolution
Compute sampling rate jitter (SD of inter‑sample interval) and synchronization offset between PPG and accelerometer
Feature misalignment index (cross‑correlation lag)
Model prediction entropy
Control variables: ambient temperature, battery voltage, firmware version, EMI exposure, casing strain
statistical_testability_builds.testable_prediction: Higher sampling rate jitter or greater synchronization offset will be associated with higher model prediction entropy.
statistical_testability_builds.failure_condition: After adjusting for ambient temperature, battery voltage, firmware version, EMI, and casing strain, the jitter/offset coefficients are not significantly positive (p>0.05).
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_test_plan: Multiple regression: entropy ~ jitter_SD + sync_offset_ms + ambient_temp + battery_voltage + firmware_version + EMI + casing_strain. Test jitter_SD and sync_offset coefficients.
statistical_testability_builds.statistical_testability_notes: Standard interpolation reduces but does not eliminate jitter; residual misalignment can be modeled as noise term.
